claims.title: Deterministic source-law information patterns obey an exact regret hierarchy
claims.scope: finite rational source-law grids, exact TV transition graphs, deterministic zero-error prefix-codebook policies, finite horizon, and one declared rational switching charge
assumptions: open-loop, delayed-feedback, current-law, and clairvoyant move orders are exactly those declared in the model
the same path-specific clairvoyant code-sequence oracle defines regret for every policy class
all bounded law, path, codebook, and Bellman enumerations complete
nonclaims: the clairvoyant benchmark is not an implementable causal policy
the hierarchy does not compare shared randomization with deterministic feedback

claims.title: Current-law feedback has zero pathwise regret when switching is free
claims.scope: the declared finite-grid zero-error prefix-codebook game with exact current-law observation and zero switching charge
assumptions: the path oracle uses the same finite codebook family
without switching cost the oracle objective decomposes period by period
the current source law is observed before the current codebook is selected
nonclaims: zero regret need not hold with positive switching cost
observing samples from the current law is not the same as observing the law exactly

claims.title: The comparator cost frontier is an exact sufficient state for feedback regret
claims.scope: the declared finite codebook family with additive expected code length and a constant per-switch charge
assumptions: frontier coordinate j is the minimum comparator prefix cost among sequences ending in codebook j
the comparator can switch among the same finite codebook family at every period
source-law and switching costs are additive across periods
nonclaims: the frontier is not proved minimal for every codebook family
frontier coordinates are not parent-substrate memory units

claims.title: Comparator-frontier updates are translation equivariant
claims.scope: the exact switching-cost frontier update over one finite codebook family
assumptions: one common scalar is added to every incoming frontier coordinate
switching and stage costs are unchanged
nonclaims: translation equivariance alone does not prove that the normalized frontier is the unique minimal state
the scalar baseline remains necessary to reconstruct the absolute oracle cost

claims.title: Pointwise dominance pruning preserves a finite rational zero-sum game
claims.scope: finite rational games where the row player maximizes and the column player minimizes
assumptions: a removed row is pointwise no larger than one retained row on all retained columns
a removed column is pointwise no smaller than one retained column on all retained rows
the reduced exact support-basis solver completes
nonclaims: the implementation does not remove a row or column using an uncertified convex-combination dominance test
pruning is a search acceleration rather than a substitute for the lifted full-matrix certificate

claims.title: Deterministic feedback-regret information value has an exact nonnegative telescope
claims.scope: any valid certificate satisfying the deterministic hierarchy zero <= current <= delayed <= open
assumptions: all four deterministic regret values use the same source-path and comparator model
nonclaims: the public-randomization gain is not inserted into the deterministic information telescope
a hybrid information-plus-randomness value requires a separately specified game

claims.title: Source-independent shared open-loop feedback regret is an exact finite rational game
claims.scope: finite-grid source paths and complete bounded open-loop code-sequence decisions with a public source-independent seed
assumptions: the source path is chosen independently of the realized shared seed
all required decoders know the realized code sequence
the lifted full regret matrix has an exact zero primal-dual game gap
nonclaims: shared open-loop randomization is not generally ordered relative to deterministic delayed or current-law feedback
the exact random-bit cost of sampling the shared mixture is not priced

claims.title: Positive switching cost can create strict regret under exact current-law feedback
claims.scope: the bounded K3 finite-grid instances exercised by the feedback-regret tests
assumptions: the designer sees the current law exactly but not future laws
the path oracle sees the complete law sequence
a positive rational codebook switching charge couples periods
nonclaims: the switching charge is a declared accounting parameter rather than a measured physical cost

claims.title: Bounded exact feedback-regret, game-pruning, and frontier audit
claims.scope: the rational source grids, paths, policy tables, codebook sequences, game matrices, and frontier states exercised by the repository tests
assumptions: all configured law, path, sequence, candidate, support-basis, and dominance caps complete without truncation
Python Fraction arithmetic is used for every finite payoff and feasibility calculation
nonclaims: bounded test completion is not a polynomial-time scalability theorem
finite feedback-regret agreement is not evidence that reality is simulated
